title: Antibiotics against gram-positive bacteria increase tumor incidence

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Antibiotics against gram-positive bacteria increase tumor incidence

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Treating Xenopus laevis embryos with antibiotics that target gram-positive bacteria — novobiocin alone, or a cocktail of gentamicin, metronidazole, vancomycin and clindamycin — significantly increases the incidence of oncogene-induced tumor-like structures, implying that native butyrate-producing bacteria normally restrain tumorigenesis.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: Transmembrane voltage potential of somatic cells controls oncogene-mediated tumorigenesis at long-range

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Chernet BT 2014, Transmembrane voltage potential of somatic cells controls oncogene-mediated tumorigenesis at long-range › RESULTS › Changes in Vmem

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: Finally, a cocktail of antibiotics (gentamicin, metrodinazole, vancomycin hydrochloride, and clindamycin hydrochloride, all at 20 μM concentration) targeting gram-positive bacteria resulted in a significant increase in ITLS incidence by 26.2% (χ2, P<0.05) (Fig. 6).

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Chernet BT, Levin M, “Transmembrane voltage potential of somatic cells controls oncogene-mediated tumorigenesis at long-range”, Oncotarget (2014), doi:10.18632/oncotarget.1935; section “RESULTS › Changes in Vmem”. Scope: Oncogene-injected Xenopus laevis embryos exposed to antibiotics in the rearing medium

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2014-tumor-07: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.65

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The incidence effect itself is directly testable from published measurements. The inference that native butyrate-producing bacteria normally restrain tumors is poorly discriminated from antibiotic off-target effects.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Recompute oncogene-induced tumor incidence under novobiocin, the antibiotic cocktail, nalidixic acid, and vehicle controls, and relate effects to measured microbiome composition and butyrate. Increased incidence in the stated treatments confirms the result; bacterial mediation needs the additional measurements.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
The reported butyrate reduction is not presented as a complete public dataset.

Antibiotics can act directly on embryos or mitochondria.

Microbiome composition was not characterized.

data existence: 0.55

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The incidence increase after the named cocktail is a published contrast with a sample statistic. The inference that native butyrate-producing bacteria normally restrain the tumors is not carried by that contrast alone, because the paper does not include a public microbiome or butyrate measurement for the same animals. Only the incidence half can be inspected now.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Compare oncogene-induced tumor incidence after novobiocin and after the stated gram-positive-targeting cocktail versus vehicle, and pair the incidence change with measured loss of butyrate-producing bacteria. An incidence increase only when those bacteria decline would support the implication; an increase without a microbiome change would leave the bacterial reading unsupported.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Bacterial composition and butyrate were not deposited for these embryo cohorts.

Antibiotics change more than gram-positive, butyrate-producing taxa.
